text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - The UK stock market ended the third quarter on a quiet but positive note, with a rout among utilities offset by selective buying of other blue chips. The FTSE 100 share index reversed modest early losses to end the day at 3,953.7 points, up 7.3 points. That brought the gain in the last three months to 242.7 points, almost the entire year's rise for the blue-chip indicator.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade lower on Monday amid evidence of profit-taking after last week's highs, but off earlier lows and keeping an eye out for U.S. data due in the afternoon. The 30-share blue chip DAX index ended down 7.19 points at 2,651.85 points. In post-bourse trade the index fell 4.37 to 2,655.49.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply higher on Monday as September futures expired in a bullish mood helped by an early rise in the Dow Jones index. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 25.76 points at 2,132.81.

ZURICH - Swiss shares shook off early weariness to close above important resistance levels of 3,700 and 3,710 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI). Dealers said the SMI future, which showed a marked rise in the afternoon, was the main reason for the market's good performance. Some window dressing and short covering may also have helped. The market may be about to leave its recent sideways movement, a trader said, adding the 3,800 level may be within reach if 3,750 points could be overcome. The all-share SPI was up 20.27 points to 2,393.34.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed modestly higher on Monday, with trading remaining quiet on the last day of the first half year of the financial year. Brokers said the market's attention was shifting to how the key stock index would move from October 1.
The key 225-share Nikkei average finished up 9.38 points at 21,556.40.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks soared ahead in Monday trade with the Hang Seng index jumping to new 1996 highs on an improved outlook for interest rates and upward revisions in corporate earnings forecasts, brokers said. "We are getting positive economic signals and stronger than expected corporate earnings," said Amy Wong, research director at New China Hong Kong Securities Ltd. The Hang Seng Index put on 143.04 points to close at 11,902.43.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed firmer on Monday after the market scrambled off its lows in the afternoon ahead of the September share index futures expiry. The All Ordinaries index gained 7.4 points to 2290.40. Brokers said a spurt of activity in the leaders in the afternoon saw the bourse head to higher ground.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares were battered on Monday by a sickly gold price which also dampened sentiment in industrial shares. Dealers said some unit trust players tried to lift the market off worst day levels after pushing the market higher at open, but it was too late to have any significant impact. "It has been erratic this last half-hour. Players were pushing and pulling prices. The market has been all over. The low gold price, which is below the key $380 (an ounce) level also triggered selling in industrials," one said.

The poor August trade surplus figure of 132 million rand also dampened sentiment in industrials and did not bode well for the unit trust close-out, dealers said. The overall index fell 55.2 points to 6,878 points, the industrial index shed 48.6 points to 8,130.6 points and the gold index dropped 43.3 points, or 2.55 percent, to 1,653.7 points.
